text.p: Following are the main stories in Slovenia's Thursday morning newspapers:
- Parliament on Wednesday ratified 25 international accords, among them several air traffic and technological cooperation agreements with various European countries.

- The Nationalist Party is pushing for a referendum to decide whether to limit the amount of forest areas that can be returned to their former owners, who lost property in the nationalisation process after World War Two.

- At present 28,000 people work in public administration, three times more than in 1991 when Slovenia broke away from the former Yugoslavia. The new government may even increase the size of state administration, experts said.
- A man who last September planted a bomb in front of a judge's house, seriously injuring his wife, was sentenced to 14 years in jail on Wendesday.
- From Thursday the oldest whistle found in Europe will be exhibited at the Slovenian National Museum. The whistle, estimated to be over 40,000 years old, was found in Slovenia two years ago.

- Inspectors removed some 600 Irish cans of beef from three Slovenian shops which breached an import ban on beef products. The ban was introduced last year in response to BSE, or "mad cow disease", fears.
